messages:
jonathan: Quick follow-up to the multi-region RFC — we need a concrete decision for how KV cache routing + failover should behave when tenants have data residency constraints. listing options and tradeoffs?
maria: +1 we should encode residency at the tenant level and enforce region-affinity. but need fallback rules for availability.
kevin: Concern: if we do async replication of kv cache active/active, clients might see slightly stale prefix completions. Is that acceptable for most customers? any SLAs targeted?
sasha: For most non-sensitive tenants eventual consistency is fine. For residency-restricted tenants we should not replicate out of-region at all; those must be pinned.
riyad: Legal note: some EU customers require data "at rest" and "in transit" to stay in EU. That rules out copying logs or kv cache outside region, even encrypted, unless explicitly allowed.
maria: Proposal: three routing classes -> "pinned", "affinity", "global".
  - pinned: never leave region, active only in-region.
  - affinity: primary region preferred, allow read-through fallback to secondaries for cold starts but writes replicate asynchronously.
  - global: fully active/active replicate across regions for availability.
kevin: What about model variants and serving fallbacks? If a model isn't deployed in EU for cost reasons, pinned tenants can't get served unless we deploy local variant.
jonathan: Right. That's an ops/cost decision: either deploy minimal compatible model to every region for pinned tenants, or return 409/route to on-prem/private for those tenants. We need a policy.
maria: Suggested routing config snippet:
```
routing:
  tenant_residency: eu
  class: affinity
  fallback_policy:
    allow_cross_region_reads: false  # for pinned tenants
    allow_model_fallback: true
    allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
```
sasha: For KV consistency: use read-through cache with per-prefix lease + vector timestamp for replication. That keeps reads fast and gives us an invalidation path.
kevin: Can we avoid cross-region synchronous writes? that kills p99 for generation. prefer async replication + tombstones. fallback can be stale but we surface warnings in console.
infra-bot: note: deploying cross-region replication will increase inter-region egress and has cost impact (~30-50% depending on traffic).
riyad: Also add KMS constraints: keys for EU-residency tenants must be EU-managed.
maria: Operational suggestion: implement a routing decision API that returns {region, residency_class, allowed_fallbacks} so serving runtime remains simple.
jonathan: Interface boundary: runtime should call a single sync decision service. decision service owns data about tenant residency, model placements, and current region capacity. keeps runtime dumb.
kevin: That makes rollout easier. We can also add a feature flag to switch "allow_cross_region_reads" per-tenant for gradual migration.
deploy-bot: canary feature-flag "routing-affinity" enabled on infra staging cluster.
maria: Action items: (1) update RFC with the 3 classes and decision-service interface (2) infra to list regions where minimal models are required for pinned tenants (3) add KMS/residency checks to onboarding flow.
jonathan: Sounds good. @maria can you own the RFC patch? i'll draft the decision-service API doc and wireframe the console UX for residency indicators.
maria: yep i'll open RFC patch this week and add examples + tests. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll prototype a small harness to validate stale read rates under async replication.
sasha: I'll sketch replication metadata (vector timestamps + tombstone + lease) and add to the RFC.
jonathan: Great discussion. We'll treat this as RFC follow-up and try not to bake into runtime until we've validated the prototype. thanks all.
